overview:
Since 2020, my professional efforts have focused on decreasing the impact of trauma on the lives of nurses and U.S. Veterans due to the mass trauma of COVID-19. In 2020, I undertook training to become certified in the Community Resiliency Model™, an evidenced-based approach in addressing primary and secondary trauma of frontline health care providers. Before 2020, I had focused on educating and increasing the psychiatric nurse practitioner workforce, especially as pertaining to Veterans' mental health. A primary focus was on meaningful recovery from trauma for Veterans due to 20 years of armed conflicts in Iraq and Afghanistan. While remaining an important continued focus, another battle is being waged today against secondary traumatic stress experienced by front line nurses and other first responders. I have taught Community Resiliency Model™ sessions via Zoom and in person for nurses, law enforcement, and educators to improve their personal resiliency skills and decrease trauma.

Historically, my scholarship focused on vulnerable youth who have been internationally adopted from orphanages as well as risk and protective factors for children in U.S. foster care. Additionally, myteaching scholarship focuses on increasing psychiatric nursing workforce, especially as it pertains to Veterans' mental health. From 2013-2020, I served as co-director of the Mental Health Nurse Practitioner Residency, a joint program between the Birmingham VAMC and the UAB School of Nursing which educates new psychiatric nurse practitioners in Veteran-centric care. 

My current efforts include increasing the mental health workforce of Alabama which ranks 51st in the nation and the District of Columbia. Read my opinion from AL.com to improve Alabama's mental health workforce: 
https://www.al.com/opinion/2023/01/healthcare-pro-alabamas-mental-health-requires-these-steps.html?fbclid=IwAR11d80VfN_WQp6iu249dMkTJowurwhPIILAq56uR4zUyhIH9B3XhnHN2xU
